Harriet Hageman

Republican candidate for United States Senator, Wyoming · Open seat

U.S. Representative for Wyoming's at-large district; attorney

Harriet Hageman is a Republican who has represented Wyoming's at-large district in the U.S. House since January 2023, after more than 30 years as a water, natural resources and constitutional trial attorney. She is running for the U.S. Senate seat held by retiring Sen. Cynthia Lummis. She won the Republican nomination in the August 18, 2026 primary and faces Democrat James Byrd in the November 3, 2026 general election.

Where Hageman stands

Energy and regulation
Says Wyoming's energy and mineral resources should be central to national energy policy. Pledges to work for regulatory reform, permitting modernization, local infrastructure funding and highway safety.
Healthcare
Points to more than $205 million she says she secured for Wyoming through the Rural Health Transformation Program. Says any national healthcare reform should account for how care is delivered in rural areas.
Public lands
Supports a "multiple use and sustained yield" approach to federal lands that prioritizes access, responsible development and conservation, with local input in management decisions.
Immigration
Supports a closed border, legal entry only, and selective immigration based on education, qualifications and willingness to assimilate. Says Congress should keep border security funded while deportations focus on criminal offenders first.
Tribal affairs
Supports tribal autonomy. Introduced legislation to extend tribal land lease terms from 25 to 99 years and says she secured $1 million for the Arapaho wastewater system.
Senate confirmations
Says the president is entitled to choose his or her team. Says she would judge each nominee on qualifications, temperament and background, and wants judicial nominees who follow the Constitution.
Bipartisanship
Cites bills she co-led with Democrats, including the Victims' VOICES Act and the Postal Processing Protection Act. Says she will not compromise on what she calls fundamental values of limited government and the Constitution.

Background

  • U.S. Representative, Wyoming at-large district, 2023–present (term ends January 2027)
  • Chaired the House Subcommittee on Indian and Insular Affairs during her first term
  • Water, natural resources and constitutional trial attorney for more than 30 years; practiced in Michigan and Colorado 1990–1997
  • Born in Douglas, Wyoming; grew up near Fort Laramie; has lived in Cheyenne since 1997
  • Won the Republican U.S. Senate primary on August 18, 2026 with 64.9% of the vote
